title: Integrating Large Language Models with Human Data to Design Personalized Decoy Nudges
abstract: arXiv:2508.12045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Although nudge strategies can influence behavior, their effectiveness varies across individuals, highlighting the need for personalized nudge design. We hypothesize that large language models (LLMs) can facilitate the development of individual-specific nudges while reducing the financial and time costs associated with human data collection by augmenting small human samples or by replacing human participants. Using the decoy effect as a test case, we evaluate these hypotheses in a preregistered field experiment involving 3,495 participants across five countries. We show that decoy parameters identified by LLMs as optimal for a given country generate stronger nudging effects than non-optimal parameters in the United States and, marginally, in Germany, but not in China, India, or Singapore. translated_title: 将大语言模型与人类数据相结合以设计个性化诱饵助推
translated_abstract: 尽管助推策略能够影响行为，但其有效性因人而异，这凸显了个性化助推设计的必要性。我们假设大语言模型（LLMs）可以通过扩充小规模人类样本或替代人类被试，来促进个体特异性助推的开发，同时降低人类数据收集的经济与时间成本。以诱饵效应作为测试案例，我们在一项涉及五个国家、3,495名参与者的预注册现场实验中检验了这些假设。结果表明，由大语言模型识别出的针对特定国家的最优诱饵参数，在美国产生了比非最优参数更强的助推效果，在德国也有边际显著的效果，但在中国、印度或新加坡则没有。我们没有发现证据表明基于大语言模型的个性化诱饵比国家层面的最优诱饵产生更强的助推效果。
tldr: 一项覆盖五国、3495名参与者的预注册现场实验表明，大语言模型虽能识别出国家层面的最优诱饵参数从而增强助推效果，但无法可靠地生成优于国家层面策略的个性化诱饵助推。
en_tdlr: A preregistered field experiment with 3,495 participants across five countries shows that while LLMs can identify country-level optimal decoy parameters that strengthen nudging effects, they fail to reliably generate personalized decoy nudges that outperform country-level strategies.
